title: Single number II
statement: Every element appears three times except one, which appears once. Find it in O(n) time and O(1) extra space. Values are 32-bit signed integers.
hints: Count, for each bit position, how many numbers have that bit set: the counts are ≡ the single number's bit (mod 3).
The ones/twos trick is that per-bit mod-3 counter in two words.

solution.explanation: Generalise XOR (which is addition mod 2 per bit) to per-bit counting mod 3. The direct version loops over 32 bit positions; the two-word version (ones, twos) is a 2-bit counter per position that resets at 3. Python integers are unbounded, so with negative numbers the per-bit version must convert back from 32-bit two's complement; the ones/twos version works as is.
solution.cpp: int singleNumber(vector<int>& a) { int ones = 0, twos = 0; for (int x : a) { ones = (ones ^ x) & ~twos; twos = (twos ^ x) & ~ones; } return ones; }
